subject: maths
title: 3-D Objects: Faces, Edges, Vertices and Surfaces
seo_title: Year 3 3-D Objects Worksheets: Faces, Edges, Vertices, Prisms and Pyramids (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Make, compare and classify objects, identifying key features and explaining why these features make them suited to their uses
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on 3-D objects: name cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones and spheres in any position, count faces, edges and vertices, sort objects that roll, slide or stack, and make models with straws and connectors. 100 questions with an answer key, following the Australian Curriculum.
key_big: Faces, edges and vertices describe an object. Flat faces stack and slide; curved surfaces roll.
key_sub: A face is a flat surface, an edge is where two faces meet, and a vertex is a corner. Count the faces you cannot see too. A prism has the same shape at both ends; a pyramid comes to a point.

faq.q: What 3-D objects do Year 3 students learn in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Cubes, rectangular prisms, triangular prisms, square-based pyramids, cylinders, cones and spheres. Students name their faces, edges and vertices and explain why their features suit their uses (AC9M3SP01).

faq.q: What is the difference between a face, an edge and a vertex?
faq.a: A face is a flat surface, an edge is where two faces meet, and a vertex is a corner where edges meet. A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.

faq.q: What is the difference between a prism and a pyramid?
faq.a: A prism has the same shape at both ends, joined by rectangles, so it has no point. A pyramid has one base and triangle faces that meet at a point.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn 3-D objects at home?
faq.a: Hunt for objects in the kitchen, such as a tin (cylinder) or a cereal box (rectangular prism), and test which ones roll, slide or stack. Building objects with straws and connectors or modelling clay helps too.

items.e: It has 6 faces and they are all squares of the same size, so it is a cube. It is turned, but it is still a cube.

items.q: Name this 3-D object.
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. It is turned so you see a triangle end at the front. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.

items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. Turning an object does not change its name.

items.q: What is this object called?
items.e: It has a square face at the bottom and 4 triangle faces that meet at a point, so it is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a cube. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too. Do not forget the vertex at the top.

items.q: This is a cube. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: How many vertices does a rectangular prism have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 8 vertices: 4 at the top and 4 at the bottom. 12 is the number of edges.

items.q: Which 2-D shapes are the faces of a triangular prism?
items.e: A triangular prism has a triangle at each end (2 triangles) and 3 rectangles joining them: 5 faces.

items.q: This is a cube. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: A flat surface of an object is called a …
items.e: A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner.

items.q: The line where two faces of an object meet is called an …
items.e: Where two faces meet there is an edge.

items.q: Which object has 5 vertices?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 4 vertices round the square and 1 at the top: 4 + 1 = 5. A triangular prism has 6.

items.q: Zara counts 12 on a rectangular prism. She is right. What did she count?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. So 12 is the number of edges.

items.q: Which 2-D shapes are the faces of a square-based pyramid?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 1 square at the bottom and 4 triangles that meet at the top: 5 faces.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: A corner of an object, where edges meet, is called a …
items.e: A corner is a vertex. More than one vertex are called vertices.

items.q: Leo says a cube has 8 edges. He is wrong. What did he count?
items.e: A cube has 8 vertices (corners) and 12 edges. Leo counted the vertices.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

sets.title: Flat and curved surfaces: roll, slide or stack

items.e: A cone has 1 flat circle face at the bottom. The rest is a curved surface that comes to a point.

items.q: Which object is best for building a tall, steady tower?
items.e: A cube has flat faces on top and underneath, so cubes sit flat on each other. Spheres roll off, and you cannot stack on a point.

items.q: Which object has only flat surfaces?
items.e: A cube has 6 flat faces and no curved surface. A cylinder, a cone and a sphere all have a curved surface.

items.q: Which object can roll and can also slide?
items.e: A cylinder rolls on its curved surface and slides on a flat face. Objects with only flat faces cannot roll.

items.q: Why can you not stack a block on top of a square-based pyramid?
c: It comes to a point at the top.
items.e: The 4 triangle faces meet at a point at the top, so there is no flat face for a block to sit on.

items.q: Which object has only a curved surface?
items.e: A sphere is curved all over. It has no flat faces, no edges and no vertices.

items.q: Which object has 2 flat faces and 1 curved surface?
items.e: A cylinder has a flat circle face at each end and 1 curved surface round the side. A cone has only 1 flat face.

items.q: Which object can slide but cannot roll?
items.e: A rectangular prism has only flat faces, so it slides. Objects with a curved surface can roll.

c: It rolls in a straight line.
It rolls round in a circle.
items.e: Lying on its curved surface, a cylinder rolls in a straight line. A cone rolls round in a circle and a sphere rolls in every direction.

items.q: Which object can roll in every direction?
items.e: A sphere is curved all over, so it can roll any way you push it. A cylinder rolls only in a straight line.

items.q: Leo sorts objects into “rolls” and “does not roll”. Which object goes in “does not roll”?
items.e: A triangular prism has only flat faces, so it does not roll. A cylinder, a cone and a sphere have a curved surface.
A is a rectangular prism. All 6 of its faces are flat. The others each have a curved surface.

items.q: How many surfaces does a cone have altogether?
items.e: A cone has 1 flat face (the circle) and 1 curved surface: 1 + 1 = 2 surfaces.

items.q: Can you stack cylinders?
c: Yes, if they stand on their flat faces.
Yes, if they lie on their sides.
items.e: A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces. Standing on them, cylinders stack like tins on a shelf.

items.q: Zara has a cube, a cylinder, a sphere, a cone and a rectangular prism. How many of them can roll?
items.e: The cylinder, the sphere and the cone have curved surfaces, so they can roll: 3 objects. The cube and the rectangular prism cannot.

c: It rolls round in a circle.
items.e: It is standing on a flat circle face, so it slides. It can roll only when it lies on its curved surface.
A cylinder has 1 curved surface that goes all the way round. The 2 circles at the ends are flat faces, not curved surfaces.

c: It rolls in a straight line.
It rolls round in a circle.
items.e: The point of the cone stays in one place and the wide end goes round it, so a cone rolls round in a circle.
D is a cylinder. It has a curved surface, so it can roll. The other objects have only flat faces.

items.q: Why is it hard to stack one sphere on top of another?
c: It has no flat face to sit on.
items.e: A sphere has only a curved surface. There is no flat face to sit on, so it rolls off.

sets.title: Classify and compare: prisms and pyramids

items.q: Which has more vertices, a triangular prism or a square-based pyramid?
items.e: A triangular prism has 6 vertices and a square-based pyramid has 5. 6 is more than 5.

items.q: How is a cylinder different from a cone?
c: A cylinder has 2 circle faces; a cone has 1.
A cylinder comes to a point.
A cone has no curved surface.
items.e: A cylinder has a flat circle face at each end. A cone has only 1 circle face and a point at the other end.

items.q: How is a cone like a square-based pyramid?
c: Both can roll in a straight line.
items.e: A cone and a pyramid both narrow to a point at the top. A cone has a circle base; a pyramid has a square base.

items.q: Which object is a prism?
items.e: A prism has the same shape at both ends, joined by rectangles. A rectangular prism has rectangle ends.

items.q: Which object has 8 edges and 5 vertices?
items.e: A square-based pyramid: 4 edges round the base and 4 up to the point (8), 4 vertices round the base and 1 at the top (5).

items.q: Which picture shows a pyramid?
items.e: C is a square-based pyramid: its triangle faces meet at a point. The others are prisms.

items.q: A prism has the same shape at both ends. What shape are the ends of a triangular prism?
items.e: A triangular prism is named after its ends: 2 triangles. The 3 faces joining them are rectangles.

items.q: Is a cube a prism?
c: No, a prism must have triangles.
Yes, it is a special rectangular prism.
No, it has a curved surface.
items.e: A cube has the same square at both ends, joined by squares. It is a rectangular prism with all faces the same size.

items.q: What is the same about these two objects?
items.e: The triangular prism has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles: 5 faces. The pyramid has 1 square and 4 triangles: 5 faces. Their vertices (6 and 5) and edges (9 and 8) are different.

items.q: Which two objects have the same number of faces, edges and vertices?
c: a cube and a rectangular prism
a triangular prism and a cube
a cube and a square-based pyramid
items.e: A cube and a rectangular prism both have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Only the shape of their faces is different.

items.q: Which object has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices?
items.e: A triangular prism: 2 triangles and 3 rectangles (5 faces), 9 edges and 6 vertices.

items.q: What is the difference between a prism and a pyramid?
c: A pyramid has no flat faces.
A prism has a curved surface.
A prism comes to a point; a pyramid does not.
A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.
items.e: The triangle faces of a pyramid meet at a point (the apex). A prism has the same shape at both ends, so it has no point.

items.q: Which object has the most edges?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges, a triangular prism has 9, a square-based pyramid has 8 and a cylinder has 2 curved edges.

items.q: Square-based pyramid, cone, sphere, cylinder. Which is the odd one out, and why?
c: the square-based pyramid: it has no curved surface
the cone: it has no point
the sphere: it has 1 flat face
items.e: The cone, sphere and cylinder each have a curved surface. The pyramid has only flat faces. The other reasons are not true.

items.q: Which object is a pyramid?
items.e: A pyramid has a base and triangle faces that meet at a point. A square-based pyramid has a square base.

items.q: Which group has only prisms?
items.e: A cube, a triangular prism and a rectangular prism all have the same shape at both ends. A pyramid and a cone come to a point.
D is a triangular prism: it has the same triangle at both ends. The others are a pyramid, a cone and a sphere.

items.q: Which has more faces, a cube or a square-based pyramid? How many more?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces and a square-based pyramid has 5. 6 − 5 = 1, so the cube has 1 more face.

items.q: Cube, cylinder, rectangular prism, triangular prism. Which is the odd one out, and why?
c: the rectangular prism: it has no vertices
the triangular prism: it can roll
the cylinder: it has a curved surface
items.e: The cube and the two prisms have only flat faces. The cylinder is the only one with a curved surface. The other reasons are not true.

items.q: How is a cube different from a rectangular prism?
c: All the faces of a cube are the same size.
items.e: Both have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. A cube is special: all 6 faces are squares of the same size.

sets.title: Objects in real life and making models

items.q: A cereal box is shaped like which object?
items.e: A cereal box has 6 rectangle faces that are not all squares, so it is a rectangular prism.

items.q: Grace makes a cube from straws and connectors. How many straws does she need?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges, so Grace needs 12 straws. 8 is the number of vertices (connectors). Each straw makes an edge and each connector makes a vertex.

items.q: Lachlan makes a square-based pyramid from straws and connectors. What does he need?
items.e: Edges: 4 round the square and 4 up to the top = 8 straws. Vertices: 4 round the square and 1 at the top = 5 connectors.

items.q: Aarav makes 2 cubes from straws and connectors. How many straws does he use?
items.e: 1 cube needs 12 straws (12 edges). 2 cubes: 12 + 12 = 24 straws. 16 counts the vertices (8 + 8) instead.

items.q: Liam has 6 connectors and 9 straws. He uses them all to make one object. Which object?
items.e: 6 vertices and 9 edges: that is a triangular prism. A square-based pyramid has 5 vertices and 8 edges.

items.q: Which object can you NOT make from straight straws and connectors?
items.e: A sphere is curved all over and has no edges or vertices, so straight straws cannot make it.

items.q: A tin of baked beans is shaped like which object?
items.e: A tin has 2 circle ends and a curved side, so it is a cylinder.

items.q: A drink can is a cylinder. Which feature lets it stand up in the fridge?
items.e: The can stands on a flat circle face at the bottom. On its curved surface it would roll.

items.q: A netball is a sphere. Why is that a good shape for a ball?
c: It bounces and rolls the same way in every direction.
It has flat faces to catch.
items.e: A sphere is curved all over, so it rolls and bounces evenly whichever way it lands.

items.q: Why is a traffic cone shaped like a cone?
c: So it can stand on its point.
So it has lots of vertices.
Its wide, flat base helps it stand up.
items.e: A traffic cone stands on its wide circle face, so it is steady. It is narrow at the top, so empty cones also fit inside each other.

items.q: Noah makes a rectangular prism from straws and connectors. How many connectors does he need?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 8 vertices: 4 at the top and 4 at the bottom. 12 is the number of edges (straws). Each straw makes an edge and each connector makes a vertex.

items.q: Isla makes a triangular prism and a square-based pyramid. How many connectors does she use altogether?
items.e: A triangular prism has 6 vertices and a square-based pyramid has 5. 6 + 5 = 11 connectors. 17 adds the edges (9 + 8).

items.q: A tin of baked beans has a paper label all the way round. Which part of the tin does the label cover?
items.e: The label goes round the side of the tin. That is the curved surface of the cylinder. The 2 flat faces are the top and bottom.

items.q: A party hat that comes to a point is shaped like which object?
items.e: It has a circle at the bottom, a curved side and a point at the top, so it is a cone.

items.q: Ava has 20 straws. She makes one cube. How many straws are left?
items.e: A cube uses 12 straws (12 edges). 20 − 12 = 8 straws left. 14 comes from taking away 6 faces instead of 12 edges.

items.q: Why are wheels round?
c: So they stand still on a hill.
So they stack in a tower.
items.e: A round wheel has no vertices or flat sides to bump on, so it rolls smoothly along the road.

items.q: Jack says a drink can is a circle. What should he say?
items.e: A circle is a flat 2-D shape. The ends of a can are circles, but the whole can is a 3-D object: a cylinder.

items.q: This model is made from straws and connectors. Which object is it?
items.e: It has 9 straws (edges) and 6 connectors (vertices). 2 triangles at the ends are joined by 3 straws, so it is a triangular prism.

items.q: Most boxes are rectangular prisms. Why is this a good shape for boxes?
c: Their flat faces stack with no gaps.
items.e: Flat faces and square corners let boxes sit on top of and next to each other with no gaps, in a truck or on a shelf.

items.q: A tent with a triangle at each end is shaped like which object?
items.e: 2 triangle ends joined by rectangles make a triangular prism.
